title: Local File Inclusion via include/require
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x; allow_url_include is Off by default (no remote include), allow_url_fopen is On by default (stream wrappers usable in file functions)
security_mechanism: include/require execute the file their argument resolves to with full application privileges, so a path assembled from input is arbitrary code execution whenever the attacker can plant PHP content anywhere the web user reads (upload directories, session files, /tmp). Even without remote include, file functions honor stream wrappers: php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=... returns application source, and data:// yields inline content to file_get_contents/fopen because allow_url_fopen is On by default. move_uploaded_file() does not inspect content or type, so an attacker-chosen destination plus an uploaded .php payload combine into the same execution primitive.

source_sink_clues.source: GET/POST/cookie page or template parameters, uploaded file names and destination paths, import/export path options.
source_sink_clues.sink: include/require with a dynamic path; file_get_contents/fopen on an attacker string while allow_url_fopen is on; move_uploaded_file into an attacker-influenced location

tracking_guards: Require a fixed allowlist mapping request keys to constant file paths; where a path is unavoidable, require basename() plus realpath containment inside a directory holding no executable or attacker-writable files; require stream wrappers to be rejected (validated realpath, no scheme prefix) before any file function; require server-generated upload names.
not_candidate_when: The included file is resolved through a fixed allowlist dictionary, realpath containment confines the result to a non-executable, non-attacker-writable directory, or upload destinations are generated server-side with content-type validation independent of client headers.
public_references: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/98.html
CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
PHP manual: supported protocols and wrappers — https://www.php.net/manual/en/wrappers.php
